test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Mid-Range Full Test - 01
subject: general
question: If the circumference of a circle is equal to the perimeter of a square, and the radius of the given circle is positive, then which of the following options is correct?

options.text: Area of the circle > Area of the square
Area of the circle ≥ Area of the square
Area of the circle = Area of the square

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2D figures having the exact same given perimeter, the figure with the greater number of sides encloses a larger area.

A circle can be considered a regular polygon with an infinite number of sides.

Thus, a circle always encloses the maximum possible area for a fixed perimeter compared to any other polygon.

Since the square and the circle have equal perimeters, the circle will enclose the greater area.

**∴ The correct answer is Area of the circle > Area of the square.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the radius of the given circle be r and the side of the square be a.

 
 
• 
 r
 
 Area = π × r²
 Circumference = 2πr
 
 
 a
 Area = a²
 Perimeter = 4a
 
 

 Equal

⇒ Circumference of the circle = 2 × π × r

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 4 × a

⇒ Given that circumference is equal to perimeter: 2 × π × r = 4 × a

⇒ Side of the square (a) = (2 × π × r) ÷ 4 = (π × r) ÷ 2

⇒ Area of the circle (A꜀) = π × r²

⇒ Area of the square (Aₛ) = a² = [(π × r) ÷ 2]² = (π² × r²) ÷ 4

⇒ Ratio of their areas (A꜀ ÷ Aₛ) = (π × r²) ÷ [(π² × r²) ÷ 4]

⇒ A꜀ ÷ Aₛ = 4 ÷ π

⇒ Since π ≈ 3.14, the value of 4 ÷ 3.14 is greater than 1.

⇒ Therefore, A꜀ > Aₛ (Since r is positive, area cannot be zero).

**∴ The correct answer is Area of the circle > Area of the square.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isoperimetric Inequality

For any closed curve of a given fixed perimeter, the circle is the unique shape that encloses the maximum possible area.

Regular Polygons with Same Perimeter

If different regular polygons have the exact same perimeter, the polygon with the greater number of sides always has a larger area (e.g., Equilateral Triangle < Square < Regular Pentagon < Regular Hexagon).

Shapes with Same Area

Conversely, if a circle and any regular polygon have the same given area, the circle will always have the minimum possible perimeter.
